resolution_rule: Use the official U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve/CMT table for 2026-08-28. Resolve TRUE if the published 10-year value is 4.70% or higher at Treasury's published precision, otherwise FALSE. Score the 0.47 probability with Brier and log loss; score the 4.69 point estimate by absolute error against the same value; compare point error with the frozen 4.67 no-change and 4.68 one-day recent-trend benchmarks; record 80% interval coverage. Do not substitute intraday market quotes or later corrections unless Treasury revises the dated official value before scoring.
rationale: H003 remains the narrow leader at 0.35, and several Fed officials used Jackson Hole to emphasize persistent inflation risk, creating upside yield risk around Chair Warsh's Aug. 28 remarks.
The official Aug. 27 10-year yield is only 4.67% and monthly core inflation was contained at 0.2%, so a >=4.70% event is kept slightly below even rather than treated as a base case.

P000020's failure reduced the recession/labor-stress branch, which makes a large safe-haven rally less likely, but one-day yield movement remains multiply determined by policy communication, inflation expectations, term premium, positioning and Treasury-specific factors.
The forecast is designed to test whether the current inflation/policy-constraint state produces an observable long-yield repricing after the highest-profile near-term policy communication event.
surprising_if: The 10-year CMT is >=4.82%, indicating much stronger policy/term-premium pressure than the forecast distribution expects.
The 10-year CMT is <=4.56% despite hawkish inflation commentary, indicating a much stronger benign/disinflation or growth-risk/rate-relief response than expected.
